source.title: Low Curvature Activations Reduce Overfitting in Adversarial Training
source.authors: Vasu Singla; Sahil Singla; S. Feizi; David W. Jacobs

record.tranche_reason: The study tests model-width double descent and training-time test-error behavior in adversarially trained networks, finding that the width-wise curve depends on the activation and that the epoch-wise double-descent shape is not established.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own activation and width experiments. It also cites earlier double-descent results, which are not recorded as rows. The width factors used in the sweep are reported, but no numeric curve values are given in the text.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own width sweep of adversarially trained WideResNet-28 models (ReLU vs SiLU) and plots robust test error per epoch for ResNet-18. This bears on V1, and loosely on V2, in a new setting: robust error under PGD adversarial training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that low-curvature activations reduce robust and standard generalization gaps and mitigate the width-wise double descent seen for ReLU. They also note that at large widths ReLU reaches the same robust error as SiLU, so the benefit fades with width.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies activation functions while adversarially training image classifiers, then examines robust generalization over epochs and model width; it is not a direct reproduction of the original double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The width-wise double-descent result depends on activation: it is reported for ReLU but not SiLU. The paper also reports that robust overfitting varies with activation curvature.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-curvature activations (SiLU) remove the width-wise robust-error peak, acting like a regularizer. At large width, ReLU reaches the same error as SiLU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The model-wise double-descent peak in adversarial training depends on activation curvature; low-curvature activations suppress it without explicit regularization tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2021
record.problems: The width-sweep results are presented as a plot without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The study reports the width-wise sweep for only ReLU and SiLU, noting that experiments with other activations were too expensive.

untested.parts: Standard (clean) test error vs width; location of the peak relative to the interpolation threshold; activations other than ReLU/SiLU.
Epoch-wise curves under the original setup (constant LR or Adam, label noise, long training); epoch curves across model sizes.
No label-noise variation, no tuned-regularization sweep, no multiple peaks.

missing.what: Standard (clean) test error/loss over epochs keeps decreasing for all activations: no fall-rise-fall in standard error.
Best-val vs final robust and standard accuracy per activation, including the CIFAR-100 rows.
SiLU at width factor 4 matches ReLU at width factor 15. Final ReLU error at large width equals SiLU's lowest.

record.verdict_notes: Fig. 7 is the authors' own experiment, though they attribute the ReLU double descent to Rice et al. The epoch-wise rows reflect robust overfitting under a step LR schedule, which is weak evidence on V2. The robust-error setting differs from the originals' standard test error, hence T3.

versions.untested_parts: Tests robust error in adversarially trained WideResNet models, not standard test error generally; the text does not locate the interpolation threshold.
Tests robust test-error behavior during adversarial training, not the general epoch-wise test-error curve across ordinary deep-network training settings.
The study does not vary training sample size.
The experiments use deep residual networks and do not test double descent across model classes.
The study does not test whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
The study does not vary label noise or test optimally tuned regularization or multiple descent peaks.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model width using different width factors
rows.note: The authors state that the width-wise double-descent phenomenon is observed for ReLU. Each plotted point averages the last 3 epochs.
rows.check: Subject should be WideResNet-28 on CIFAR-10. The measure is robust (PGD) test error, not standard test error. Values are figure-only (about 0.48–0.54 range). The interpolation threshold is not located.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model width using different width factors
rows.note: The authors state that robust test performance continues to decrease with width for SiLU, so the width-wise double-descent pattern is not observed. Each plotted point averages the last 3 epochs.
rows.check: Subject should be WideResNet-28. SiLU never fits the robust training set (final robust train accuracy is about 56% for ResNet-18), so the threshold may lie outside the sweep. Absent applies only within widths 2–15.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure robust test-error trajectory over training epochs
rows.note: The text describes robust test error as briefly decreasing around learning-rate drops and then increasing as training continues; it does not report a later descent. ReLU is the baseline activation.
rows.check: Robust test error falls, then rises after LR drops; no second descent within 200 epochs. The step LR schedule confounds the shape. Table 1 gives best-val vs final robust test accuracy (51.06 vs 49.25), and the row should carry these numbers.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure robust test-error trajectory over training epochs
rows.note: The text describes the robust test-error pattern as brief decreases around learning-rate drops followed by an increase during continued training; no later descent is reported.
rows.check: Fall-then-rise with no second descent. Table 1 numbers missing: best-val vs final robust test accuracy 50.31 vs 47.21, a 3.1% overfitting gap.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure robust test-error trajectory over training epochs
rows.note: The text describes the robust test-error pattern as brief decreases around learning-rate drops followed by an increase during continued training; no later descent is reported.
rows.check: Fall-then-rise with no second descent. Table 1 numbers missing: robust accuracy 50.15 best-val vs 49.31 final.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure robust test-error trajectory over training epochs
rows.note: The text describes the robust test-error pattern as brief decreases around learning-rate drops followed by an increase during continued training; no later descent is reported.
rows.check: The rise is small (49.62 best-val vs 49.18 final robust accuracy). No second descent.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure robust test-error trajectory over training epochs
rows.note: The text says low-curvature activations have less robust overfitting; it does not describe a later second descent in robust test error.
rows.check: For SiLU, robust test loss keeps decreasing (Fig. 1). The overfitting gap is 0.5% (49.41 vs 48.91), so there is essentially no rise and no epoch-wise double-descent shape.

source_check.correct: state=partial. SiLU robust test accuracy is 49.41% at the validation-selected checkpoint and 48.91% finally. Section 4.2 reports reduced robust overfitting, with a 0.5 percentage-point decline; it does not establish negligible or nonsignificant error growth. Figure 1's decreasing robust loss is a different measure.
source_check.problem: The absent state overlooks the reported small robust-accuracy decline and conflates loss with error.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly tests whether activation choice mitigates double descent and reports that the ReLU result fails for SiLU. Its central claim-bearing result qualifies the phenomenon, matching T5.

source_check.notes: WideResNet subjects can be specified as WideResNet-28. Do not transfer ResNet-18 training accuracy to the width sweep; the authors' conclusion about reduced gaps and convergence of large-width ReLU/SiLU performance is supported.

statements.correction: WideResNet-28; CIFAR-10; ReLU versus SiLU; PGD-10 adversary; ReLU width-wise double descent; Figure 7 values figure-only; each point averages the last 3 epochs; no reported width-20 result; code link provided.
statements.problem: The qualitative ReLU width result is supported. The 51.4% and 48.8% errors at widths 10 and 20 are not reported here; their attribution to this study cannot be verified.

statements.correction: Figure 7: SiLU WideResNet-28 robust test error decreases with width; no double-descent peak reported. WideResNet-28 robust interpolation threshold not reported. Table 1: SiLU ResNet-18 final robust training accuracy 56.15%.
statements.problem: Monotonic SiLU robust-error improvement is supported, but the claim that the WideResNet-28 sweep never reaches robust interpolation is not established. The available SiLU training accuracy concerns ResNet-18.
